title: Building Sum Formula for Depth Preservation
body_html:
Building Sum Formula for Depth Preservation

Let \(x\in B(G)\) be a rational building point and suppose the jumps of its lattice function lie in \((1/m)\mathbb Z\). For \(r\in(1/m)\mathbb Z\), the \(G_{x,r+}\)-fixed vectors in the oscillator representation can be written as the sum \[ S^{G_{x,r+}}= \sum_{y\in B(G')_{2m}} S_{B_{x,y,r/2}}, \] where \(B(G')_{2m}\) denotes target building points with jumps in \((1/(2m))\mathbb Z\).

This formula gives a short proof of depth preservation: if a theta lift is nonzero, then the depth of the target representation is at most the depth of the source; applying the same argument in the opposite direction gives equality.
proof_html:
The inclusion from right to left is immediate: each summand \(S_{B_{x,y,r/2}}\) is fixed by \(G_{x,r+}\) by the lattice-model action formula.

For the reverse inclusion, write \(r=k/m\). Fix a target point \(x'\in B(G')_{2m}\). The oscillator model is the union of subspaces \[ S_{B_{x,x',j/(2m)}}\qquad (j\ge k). \] The fixed-vector descent lemma supercuspidal_theta.fixed_vector_descent_lemma is the descent step: if a vector in \(S_{B_{x,x',j/(2m)}}\) is \(G_{x,r+}\)-fixed, then it is contained in a sum of spaces \[ S_{B_{x,y,(j-1)/(2m)}} \] as \(y\) ranges over \(B(G')_{2m}\). The descent proof uses the character formula for the action of \(G_{x,r}\) on a coset \(w+B_{x,x',0}\). Fixedness forces \(M(w)\in\mathbf g_{x,r+}\). From this condition one forms an \(o_D\)-module function \(N_t=(w+B_{x,x',0})L_{x,t+r/2}\) on \(V'\), and supercuspidal_theta.module_function_self_dual_envelope embeds it in a self-dual lattice function \(L_y'\). This gives the desired containment in \(B_{x,y,(j-1)/(2m)}\).

Iterating the descent lemma lowers \(j\) to \(k\), so every \(G_{x,r+}\)-fixed vector lies in the displayed sum over \(y\). This proves the building-sum formula. If \(\pi\) has depth \(r\) and its theta lift is nonzero, an intertwining map from the oscillator representation sends some \(S_{B_{x,y,r/2}}\) nontrivially to the target representation; hence the target has \(G'_{y,r+}\)-fixed vectors and has depth at most \(r\). Applying the same argument with \(G\) and \(G'\) interchanged gives the opposite inequality.
